quiz.q: Which program do you use to download and install Unreal Engine 5?
choices: Steam
The Epic Games Launcher, in the Unreal Engine tab under Library
The Microsoft Store
A zip file that someone sends you in a chat
quiz.explain: Unreal Engine is installed from the Epic Games Launcher. Its Library tab is where you add, update and remove engine versions.

quiz.q: During the install, the Options button lets you untick target platforms such as Android or iOS. Why is it a good idea to untick the ones you do not use?
choices: Because they cost money
Because they take a lot of disk space and you do not need them yet
Because they break Lumen
Because they only work on Linux
quiz.explain: Each extra platform adds many gigabytes to the install. You can add a platform later, when you actually want to build your game for it.

quiz.q: Can you have more than one version of Unreal Engine installed on the same computer?
choices: No, only one version at a time
Yes, they sit side by side in the Library
Only if you build the engine from source code
Only on a Mac
quiz.explain: The Library can hold several engine versions at once. This is why you always say which version you used when you send your work.

quiz.q: You launch the engine for the first time. Which screen opens first?
choices: The Level Editor
The Project Browser
The Material Editor
Fortnite
quiz.explain: The Project Browser opens first. It is the window where you open a project you already have, or create a new one.

quiz.q: Why should you say which Unreal Engine version you use when you send your work or ask for help?
choices: There is no reason to
Menus and features differ between versions, so a helper needs to know which one you have
So that the site can update your engine
Because only one version is allowed
quiz.explain: Unreal changes from version to version. A menu or an asset that exists in one version can be missing or renamed in another, so the version is the first thing a helper needs to know. Unrealcraft teaches the current UE5 version.

checklist: Open any project, or create one from the Third Person template. Open a room level of your own, or build a simple closed room in a new level from cubes: a floor, four walls and a ceiling. Set the exposure to a fixed value: add a Post Process Volume, tick Infinite Extent (Unbound), and set Metering Mode to Manual in its Exposure section. Exposure is how bright the camera makes the picture, and a fixed value stops Unreal from adjusting it, so you can see brightness changes.
Place 2 lights and give them real-world intensities, in candela or lumens, and a realistic color temperature.

Apply an IES profile to one of the lights. Lamp makers offer IES files as free downloads on their websites. Drag one .ies file into the Content Browser to import it, then pick it in the IES Texture setting of the light. The engine also comes with a few profiles, for example Complex_IES. To see them in the list, click the settings icon of the list and turn on Show Engine Content. Compare how the light looks with the profile and without it.
Write down the intensity and the temperature you used, and where you got each value from.

Open any project, or create one from the Third Person template. Download one free IES profile from the website of a lighting manufacturer. The documentation page linked on this quest names Lithonia and Philips. Import it with the Add button of the Content Browser, or drag and drop the file. If you cannot download one, use a copy of a profile that comes with the engine, for example Complex_IES in the engine folder EngineLightProfiles. To see engine content, open the Settings menu of the Content Browser and turn on Show Engine Content.
Open the imported IES asset in the Texture Editor. Write down its Brightness, which is given in candelas, and the read-only value Texture Multiplier.

Build a dark room from cubes in a new level. Place a Point Light, a Spot Light and a Rect Light on the same wall. Under Light Profiles, assign the same IES Texture to each of them. Take a screenshot of all three.
Set the Outer Cone Angle of the Spot Light to 30, and then to 80. Watch where the profile is cut off.
On the Point Light, enable Use IES Intensity. Try IES Intensity Scale at 1.0 and at 0.25. Then disable Use IES Intensity and compare with the light's own Intensity.
In the Texture Editor, set Brightness to 0 and save. Look at the Point Light with Use IES Intensity turned on. Put the original value back afterwards.
Make one Light Function material that imitates the same shape and put it on a fourth light. Note in one line which is the cheaper way to shape a light.
